questions.question: The annual Mamallapuram Dance Festival, which includes performances of Indian Classical Dances Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathak, Mohiniattam, Odissi and Kathakali, is organised in _____.
questions.solution:
The Mamallapuram Dance Festival is a month-long event organized by the Department of Tourism of Tamil Nadu.
  • Venue: It is held against the majestic backdrop of the Shore Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site built by the Pallava dynasty.
  • Diversity: The festival serves as a global stage for all eight Indian classical dance forms, including Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, and Odissi.

questions.question: The Swachh Bharat Abhiyaan is celebrated on which Indian National festival?
questions.solution:
The Swachh Bharat Abhiyaan (Clean India Mission) was officially launched on Gandhi Jayanti (October 2nd, 2014).
  • Symbolism: The campaign aligns with Mahatma Gandhi's vision of a clean and healthy India.
  • National Event: It is celebrated across the country to promote sanitation and hygiene as a collective civic duty.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states is the vibrant temple festival Thrissur Pooram celebrated?
questions.solution:
Thrissur Pooram is considered the 'Mother of all Poorams' in Kerala.
  • Venue: It is held at the Vadakkunnathan Temple in Thrissur.
  • Highlights: The festival is famous for its competitive display of decorated elephants (Kudamattom) and a spectacular 36-hour long fireworks display.
  • Founder: It was started by Raja Rama Varma, the Maharaja of Cochin.

questions.question: The Bundi Utsav is a popular festival in________.
questions.solution:
The Bundi Utsav is a grand celebration held in the town of Bundi, Rajasthan.
  • Features: The festival includes a Shobha Yatra (procession), arts and crafts fairs, and traditional Rajasthani folk music and dance performances.
  • Significance: It is organized to showcase the rich cultural heritage and historical architecture of the Hadoti region.

questions.question: In which state is the festival of ‘Kalinga Mahotsav ’celebrated?
questions.solution:
Kalinga Mahotsav, also known as the National Festival of Martial Dances, is celebrated in Odisha.
  • Venue: It takes place at the foothills of the Dhauli Stupa, the site where the Kalinga War ended and Emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism.
  • Theme: It pays tribute to the transition from war to peace through martial art performances like Kalaripayattu and Thang-ta.

questions.question: Ali-Aye-Ligang, the spring festival, is observed on the first Wednesday of the Phagun month in the Indian state of _________.
questions.solution:
Ali-Aye-Ligang is the most vibrant spring festival of the Mising tribe in Assam.
  • Etymology: 'Ali' means root/seed, 'Aye' means fruit, and 'Ligang' means sow. It marks the start of the paddy sowing season.
  • Ritual: It features the Gumrag dance and community feasts.

questions.question: Which festival from West Bengal has found a place in the UNESCO list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
questions.solution:
In 2021, Durga Puja in Kolkata was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
  • Significance: It was recognized not just as a religious festival, but as a public performance of art and community bonding.
  • Highlights: The festival is famous for its elaborate Pandals, clay idols, and the rhythmic beats of the Dhaki (drums).

questions.question: Chapchar Kut Festival, which is celebrated in anticipation of a golden harvest, is primarily a festival from ________.
questions.solution:
Chapchar Kut is the most significant traditional festival of Mizoram.
  • Nature: It is a spring festival celebrated after the completion of Jhum cultivation (clearing of forest debris).
  • Dance: The iconic Cheraw (bamboo dance) is the main attraction of this festival.

questions.question: ‘Cheiraoba’ festival is the New Year festival celebrated in the state of ___________________.
questions.solution:
Cheiraoba (Sajibu Nongma Panba) is the lunar New Year festival of the Meitei people in Manipur.
  • Tradition: People clean their houses and climb nearby hills, signifying the climbing of the path of life toward a higher spiritual level.
  • Food: Special traditional dishes are prepared and offered to the local deities.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the festival of ‘Sanjhi’ celebrated?
questions.solution:
Sanjhi is a traditional folk art and festival celebrated in Punjab and Haryana during the Navaratri period.
  • Art Form: Women and girls create images of Goddess Sanjhi on house walls using clay and cow dung, decorating them with shells and colors.
  • Symbolism: It is celebrated for the well-being and prosperity of the family.

questions.question: Which of the following is the festival that celebrates Marathi New Year?
questions.solution:
Gudi Padwa marks the Marathi New Year and the beginning of the spring season.
  • Ritual: A 'Gudi' (a bright cloth tied to a bamboo stick with a copper pot on top) is hoisted outside houses to symbolize victory and prosperity.
  • Timing: It coincides with the first day of the Chaitra month.

questions.question: Gombe Habba, celebrated in the state of Karnataka during Navaratri, is a festival of:
questions.solution:
Gombe Habba (Doll Festival) is a unique tradition in Karnataka celebrated during the ten days of Dasara.
  • Custom: Families arrange themed tiers of dolls (Bommai Kolu) representing gods, people, and daily life.
  • Significance: It preserves the rich heritage of handcrafted wooden and clay dolls, particularly those from Channapatna.

questions.question: Uzhavar Thirunal is a farmers festival celebrated in which state?
questions.solution:
Uzhavar Thirunal is a specific name for the farmers' festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu, falling on the day of Mattu Pongal.
  • Deity: It is a day dedicated to thanking the cattle (bulls and cows) and the Sun God for a successful harvest.
  • Activity: Cattle are bathed, decorated, and fed special Pongal offerings.

questions.question: Sarhul festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Sarhul is the most important tribal festival in Jharkhand, celebrated by the Oraon, Munda, and Ho tribes.
  • Meaning: It is a worship of nature, specifically the Sal tree.
  • Ritual: It marks the beginning of the New Year when Sal trees get new flowers. Tribal people pray to the Dharti Mata (Mother Earth) for a good harvest.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a national festival of India?
questions.solution: India has only three National Festivals: Independence Day (Aug 15), Republic Day (Jan 26), and Gandhi Jayanti (Oct 2). National Unity Day (Oct 31) is a significant commemorative day but is not legally categorized as a national holiday/festival in the same tier.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the 'Thaipusam' festival held?
questions.solution:
Thaipusam is a significant Hindu festival celebrated by the Tamil community in Tamil Nadu (and globally in Malaysia and Singapore).
  • Deity: It is dedicated to Lord Murugan.
  • Ritual: Devotees often carry Kavadis (physical burdens) and pierce their skin as an act of penance and devotion.

questions.question: The celebrations for which of the following festivals are held for ten days in the month of Chingam (August/September) as per the local traditions in India?
questions.solution:
Onam is the state festival of Kerala, celebrated over ten days in the month of Chingam.
  • Legend: It commemorates the home-coming of the mythical King Mahabali.
  • Features: Celebrations include Pookalam (floral carpets), Vallam Kali (snake boat races), and the grand Onasadhya (feast).

questions.question: Bushu, Yemshe and Tokhu Emong are some of the cultural festivals celebrated by the tribal people of which state?
questions.solution:
The festivals Bushu (Kachari tribe), Yemshe (Pochury tribe), and Tokhu Emong (Lotha tribe) are all major cultural harvest festivals of Nagaland.
  • Theme: They are centered around community bonding, gratitude for the harvest, and ancestral worship.

questions.question: The Dhrang Fair is a two-day festival in __________________ and is celebrated in the honour of Saint Mekran Dada to pay homage and participate in religious rituals.
questions.solution:
The Dhrang Fair is held in the Kutch district of Gujarat.
  • Context: It is held at the ashram of Mekran Dada, a saint who served travelers in the Rann of Kutch with the help of his dog 'Motia' and donkey 'Lalia'.
  • Nature: It is a religious gathering that brings together people from across the desert region.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu as a harvest festival dedicated to the Sun God?
questions.solution:
Pongal is the four-day harvest festival of Tamil Nadu dedicated to the Sun God (Surya).
  • The Dish: A dish called 'Pongal' (boiled rice and milk) is cooked in a pot until it overflows, symbolizing abundance.
  • Days: The four days are Bhogi, Surya Pongal, Mattu Pongal, and Kaanum Pongal.

questions.question: Which is the most attractive and unique festival of Assam, where the barter system comes alive?
questions.solution:
The Junbeel Mela is a historic 3-day fair in Assam (Morigaon district) where the barter system (exchange of goods without money) is still practiced.
  • Participants: Tribal people from the hills exchange ginger, turmeric, and herbs for dry fish and rice from the people of the plains.
  • Harmony: It is a symbol of peace and harmony between the hill and plain tribes.

questions.question: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in the state of ________.
questions.solution:
The Hornbill Festival is the premier cultural event of Nagaland, held annually from December 1st to 10th.
  • Title: Often called the 'Festival of Festivals', it showcases the heritage of 17 major Naga tribes.
  • Name: It is named after the Indian Hornbill, a bird deeply revered in Naga folklore.

questions.question: The Bohag Bihu, also called the _________ Bihu is a festival of merriment and heralds, the Assamese New Year and the onset of spring.
questions.solution:
Rongali Bihu (or Bohag Bihu) is the most important of the three Bihu festivals in Assam.
  • Timing: It marks the Assamese New Year in mid-April.
  • Spirit: It is a festival of merriment, music, and the famous Bihu dance, celebrating the onset of spring.

questions.question: During the Raja festival, womanhood is celebrated. In which Indian state is this festival extremely popular?
questions.solution:
The Raja Parba (or Mithuna Sankranti) is a 3-day festival in Odisha that celebrates womanhood and the fertility of the Earth.
  • Belief: It is believed that Bhudevi (Mother Earth) undergoes menstruation during these days, so all agricultural work is suspended.
  • Tradition: Girls wear new clothes, play on swings (Doli), and eat 'Poda Pitha'.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated by the Monpas in Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
Losar is the Tibetan New Year festival celebrated by the Monpa tribe in Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Rituals: It involves cleaning houses to ward off evil spirits and traditional masked dances (Cham).
  • Context: It is primarily celebrated in the Tawang and West Kameng districts.
